groups.title: Basic Therapies
groups.intro: Electrotherapy and thermal modalities — the foundation of treatment at the clinic, often used on their own or combined in a session.

items.name: Interferential Therapy (IFT)
items.description: One of the types of electrotherapy used for the management of pain, muscle spasms and inflammation through deep tissue stimulation.

items.name: Ultrasound Therapy (US)
items.description: Deep heat produced by sound waves, used to reduce pain and stiffness and to support the healing of soft tissue.

items.name: Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS)
items.description: Mild electrical pulses applied over the painful area to help reduce pain without affecting sensation.

items.name: Electrical Muscle Stimulation (EMS)
items.description: Mild electrical pulses used to stimulate and re-activate weakened muscles and improve circulation.

items.name: Infrared Radiation (IRR)
items.description: Superficial radiant heat used to relax tight muscles and ease stiffness before hands-on treatment.

items.name: Hydrocollator Packs
items.description: Hot packs wrapped in warm moist towels, a classic modality for easing muscle spasm and joint stiffness.

items.name: Cervical & Lumbar Traction Therapy
items.description: Carefully controlled pulling force to reduce pressure on the spine and ease neck and lower back pain.

groups.title: Advanced Therapies
groups.intro: Hands-on and specialised techniques used for targeted treatment, deeper tissue work and more complex conditions.

items.name: Cupping Therapy
items.description: An ancient healing practice with a strong place in modern physiotherapy — used for pain relief, muscle recovery and improving blood flow.

items.name: Dry Needle Therapy
items.description: Also known as Trigger Point Dry Needling — a procedure using thin needles to release myofascial trigger points and relieve muscle pain.

items.name: Taping Therapy / Kinesio Taping
items.description: Elastic therapeutic tape applied over the skin to support movement, reduce pain and control swelling.

items.name: Manual Therapy
items.description: Hands-on techniques including joint mobilisation, manipulation and soft tissue work to restore movement and reduce pain.

items.name: Pelvic Floor Physical Therapy
items.description: Specialised assessment and treatment for pelvic floor muscle weakness, pain and bladder or bowel dysfunction.

items.name: Myofascial Release (MFR)
items.description: Gentle sustained pressure on tight bands in the fascia to release restriction and restore movement.

items.name: Positional Release Technique
items.description: Positioning a painful muscle in a shortened, comfortable position so it relaxes and the trigger point settles.

items.name: Soft Tissue Mobilization
items.description: Manual work on muscles and fascia to break down adhesions, improve mobility and reduce muscle pain.
